facts.statement: Akainacephalus was an ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in southern Utah during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the late Campanian stage about 76.26 million years ago.
facts.quote: Akainacephalus (meaning "thorn head") is a monospecific genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur from southern Utah that lived during the Late Cretaceous (late Campanian, 76.26 Ma)

facts.statement: The genus Akainacephalus was described in 2018 by paleontologists Jelle P. Wiersma and Randall B. Irmis.
facts.quote: It was described in 2018 by Jelle P. Wiersma and Randall B. Irmis.

facts.statement: An almost complete skeleton of Akainacephalus was excavated between 2008 and 2010 from the Horse Mountain Gryposaur Quarry in the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument, Utah.
facts.quote: An almost complete skeleton of an ankylosaurid was excavated during the 2008, 2009, and 2010 field seasons from the Horse Mountain Gryposaur (HMG) Quarry in the Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument, Kane County, Utah.

facts.statement: The geological layer containing the Akainacephalus fossils is dated to 76.26 ± 0.10 million years ago using zircon dating.
facts.quote: The age of the layer is 76.26 ± 0.10 million years based on zircon dating.

facts.statement: Researchers performed a CT scan on the Akainacephalus skull in 2014 to study its internal anatomy.
facts.quote: In 2014, the skull was subjected to a CT scan in order to reveal the internal anatomy.

facts.statement: The Akainacephalus holotype represents approximately 45% of the skeleton and is housed at the Natural History Museum of Utah in Salt Lake City.
facts.quote: It represents about 45% of the skeletal elements and is part of the collection of the Natural History Museum of Utah in Salt Lake City.

facts.statement: The name Akainacephalus means "thorn head" and refers to the thorn-like caputegulae (bony scales) on the skull.
facts.quote: The generic name, Akainacephalus, is derived from the Greek words "akaina" (thorn or spine) and "kephalè" (head), in reference to the thornlike cranial caputegulae of the holotype skull.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus johnsoni is the most complete ankylosaur specimen ever found from southern Laramidia, featuring a complete skull and tail club.
facts.quote: The type and only species, Akainacephalus johnsoni, is known from the most complete ankylosaur specimen ever discovered from southern Laramidia, including a complete skull, tail club, a number of osteoderms, limb elements and part of its pelvis, among other remains.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus is closely related to Nodocephalosaurus and shares similar cranial anatomy with it.
facts.quote: It is closely related and shares similar cranial anatomy to Nodocephalosaurus.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus possessed massive supraorbital bosses that formed a high ridge extending over the eye socket.
facts.quote: The supraorbital bosses are massive in side view, forming a high back-swept ridge, also extending sideways over the eye socket, while encompassing the front top corner and the rear edge of the eye socket.

facts.statement: The cheek horns of Akainacephalus were triangular and pointed almost vertically downward.
facts.quote: The cheek horns are triangular, pointing almost vertically to below.

facts.statement: A large, flat, hexagonal osteoderm was located centrally on the frontal bones of the skull.
facts.quote: On the frontal bones, a central large flat hexagonal osteoderm is present.

facts.statement: The area between the frontal and nasal bones was covered with closely packed, symmetrically arranged pyramid-shaped and conical caputegulae.
facts.quote: The zone spanning the frontal bones and nasal bones is covered by symmetrically positioned, closely packed, pyramid-shaped and conical caputegulae.

facts.statement: The external nostrils of Akainacephalus were fully obscured from the front and were small, tear-shaped openings, a trait rare among Asian and Laramidian ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: The external nares are fully obscured in front view, a condition not seen in many Asian and Laramidian ankylosaurids, and are relatively small, tear-shaped openings.

facts.statement: The premaxillae of Akainacephalus formed a narrow, U-shaped beak that tapered slightly toward the front.
facts.quote: The premaxillae slightly taper towards the front and form a narrow, U-shaped beak.

facts.statement: Each maxilla of Akainacephalus preserves 16 alveolar cavities for teeth.
facts.quote: The maxillae preserves 16 alveolar cavities each.

facts.statement: The postorbital horns of Akainacephalus were triangular at the back and had a rough, bulbous surface texture.
facts.quote: The postorbital horns are triangular towards the back, with a rugose and bulbous surface texture.

facts.statement: It is currently unknown whether Akainacephalus had squamosal and quadratojugal horns wider than its postorbital horns due to damage and deformation of the fossil.
facts.quote: Due to the damaged squamosal horns and more vertically oriented quadratojugal horns, it is unknown if Akainacephalus had squamosal horns and quadratojugal horns that exceeded the width of the postorbital horns.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus is a monospecific genus classified within the ankylosaurid dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Akainacephalus (meaning "thorn head") is a monospecific genus of ankylosaurid dinosaur

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus Akainacephalus is Akainacephalus johnsoni.
facts.quote: The type and only species, Akainacephalus johnsoni

facts.statement: The Horse Mountain Gryposaur Quarry is a diverse bonebed that has yielded fossils of Gryposaurus, Arvinachelys, a small alligatoroid, and a small theropod alongside Akainacephalus.
facts.quote: The Horse Mountain Gryposaur Quarry represents a multitaxic and multidominant bonebed that has produced a mostly complete, partially articulated skeleton of the hadrosaurid Gryposaurus, the holotype of the baenid turtle Arvinachelys, an articulated skeleton of a small alligatoroid, and a partial skull of a small theropod.

facts.statement: The tail club of Akainacephalus consists of a handle made of eleven fused vertebrae and a knob formed by three osteoderms.
facts.quote: The tail club is made up of the handle, which consists of eleven fused caudal vertebrae as in Dyoplosaurus, and the knob, which consists of only two lateral osteoderms and a single distal osteoderm.

facts.statement: The tail club knob has a subtriangular shape and is composed of two large and one small osteoderm.
facts.quote: The knob itself displays an overall subtriangular morphology in dorsal and ventral view, and is composed of two major osteoderms and a single minor osteoderm.

facts.statement: The femoral head of Akainacephalus is oriented horizontally, a trait shared with other Late Cretaceous Laramidian ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: The femoral head is oriented horizontally.

facts.statement: The cervical half rings of Akainacephalus are made of six fused osteoderms that lack saw-tooth sutures.
facts.quote: Each cervical half ring is composed of six individual osteoderms, which are fused to the upper surfaces of the half rings and lack saw-tooth sutures.

facts.statement: Only fourteen non-cervical osteoderms are known for Akainacephalus, and they are all tall with strongly keeled dorsal margins.
facts.quote: Only 14 noncervical osteoderms are known and are all tall with dorsal margins that are strongly keeled.

facts.statement: Type 1 osteoderms in Akainacephalus are asymmetrical with rounded apexes, and five mostly incomplete examples are known.
facts.quote: Type 1 osteoderms are represent by 5 mostly incomplete osteoderms which are asymmetrical and have rounded apexes.

facts.statement: Eight partial type 2 osteoderms are known, varying in size and featuring a slightly rugose surface with minimal pitting.
facts.quote: Type 2 osteoderms are represented by 8 partial osteoderms which all vary in size and have a surface texture which is slightly rugose with minimal pitting.

facts.statement: Wiersma and Irmis (2018) classified Akainacephalus within a southern Laramidian clade with Nodocephalosaurus, nested among Asian taxa.
facts.quote: Wiersma and Irmis (2018) found Akainacephalus to be within a southern Laramidian clade containing Nodocephalosaurus that is nested within Asian taxa rather than other Laramidian taxa

facts.statement: Park et al. (2019) placed Akainacephalus and Nodocephalosaurus as basal to Saichania, Talarurus, Tarchia, and Zaraapelta.
facts.quote: Park et al. (2019) found both Akainacephalus and Nodocephalosaurus to be basal to Saichania, Talarurus, Tarchia and Zaraapelta

facts.statement: Frauenfelder et al. (2022) recovered Akainacephalus as a sister taxon to two clades: one containing Tsagantegia, Nodocephalosaurus, and Talarurus, and another containing Saichania, Pinacosaurus, Scolosaurus, Anodontosaurus, Euoplocephalus, and Ankylosaurus.
facts.quote: Frauenfelder et al. (2022) recovered Akainacephalus as sister taxon to two clades, with one of the clades consisting of Tsagantegia, Nodocephalosaurus and Talarurus while the other consists of more deeply nested taxa such as Saichania, Pinacosaurus, Scolosaurus, Anodontosaurus, Euoplocephalus and Ankylosaurus.

facts.statement: Park et al. (2019) suggested that ankylosaurines dispersed from Asia to Western North America at least twice, with one migration occurring before the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: Park et al. (2019) found both Akainacephalus and Nodocephalosaurus to be basal to Saichania, Talarurus, Tarchia and Zaraapelta, which suggests that a migration occurred before the Cenomanian stage and that ankylosaurines dispersed at least twice from Asia to Western North America.

facts.statement: It is debated whether ankylosaurine dispersal from Asia to North America occurred once or at least twice, with Park et al. (2019) arguing for at least two separate events.
facts.quote: However, Park et al. (2019) found both Akainacephalus and Nodocephalosaurus to be basal to Saichania, Talarurus, Tarchia and Zaraapelta, which suggests that a migration occurred before the Cenomanian stage and that ankylosaurines dispersed at least twice from Asia to Western North America.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus lived approximately 76.26 million years ago during the upper Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Akainacephalus is known from the middle unit of the Kaiparowits Formation which has been dated to the upper Campanian stage, 76.26 ± 0.10 Ma.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus lived in a wet, humid climate that supported abundant and diverse life.
facts.quote: The climate was wet and humid, and supported an abundant and diverse range of organisms.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus inhabited a wet alluvial to coastal plain environment in the Western Interior of North America, characterized by large rivers, ponds, lakes, and wetlands.
facts.quote: The Kaiparowits Formation preserves a unique record of Late Cretaceous terrestrial vertebrate ecosystems in the Western Interior of North America as it was deposited in a wet alluvial to coastal plain setting that was dominated by large river channels, ponds, lakes, and wetlands.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus coexisted with various dinosaurs including Gryposaurus, Parasaurolophus, Utahceratops, Kosmoceratops, Nasutoceratops, Anodontosaurus, Hagryphus, Talos, Teratophoneus, and Skaladromeus.
facts.quote: Akainacephalus coexisted with other dinosaurs, such as the saurolophine hadrosaurid Gryposaurus monumentensis, the lambeosaurine hadrosaurid Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus, an indeterminate brachylophosaurin, the chasmosaurine ceratopsids Utahceratops and Kosmoceratops, the centrosaurine ceratopsid Nasutoceratops, the ankylosaurine ankylosaurid Anodontosaurus, an indeterminate nodosaurid, an indeterminate ornithopod, the orodromine thescelosaurid "Skaladromeus", the caenagnathid Hagryphus, the troodontid Talos, the enantiornithine avisaurid Mirarce, the tyrannosaurid Teratophoneus, and an indeterminate ornithomimid.

facts.statement: Non-dinosaur animals living alongside Akainacephalus included turtles like Boremys and Deinosuchus, and an azhdarchid pterosaur.
facts.quote: Non-dinosaur taxa contemporaneous with Akainacephalus include the baenid turtles Boremys, Arvinachelys, Denazinemys, Neurankylus and Thescelus, the paracryptodire turtle Compsemys, the adocid turtle Adocus, the nanhsiungchelyid Basilemys, the soft shell turtle Helopanoplia, the alligatoroids Deinosuchus and Leidyosuchus, and an indeterminate azhdarchid pterosaur.

"cabeza con espinas de Randy Johnson") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Akainacephalus de dinosaurio tireóforo anquilosáurido, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años, en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The generic name Akainacephalus combines the Greek words for 'spine' and 'head', referring to its spiky armor.

facts.statement: The specific name johnsoni honors Randy Johnson, the specimen's preparator.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a Randy Johnson su preparador.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus had massive supraorbital protuberances forming a high crest extending backward and laterally over the eye cavity.

facts.statement: A large, flat, central hexagonal osteoderm is present on the frontal bones.

facts.statement: The main armor of Akainacephalus is surprisingly similar to that of the related Nodocephalosaurus, found in southern Laramidia, New Mexico.

facts.statement: In Akainacephalus, the front and rear supraorbital osteoderms form a single high structure sweeping backward.

facts.statement: The front and premaxillary jaw bones form a wide, U-shaped beak that is wider than it is long.

facts.statement: The number of maxillary teeth per side is estimated to be at least sixteen.

facts.statement: The square bone is strongly inclined, positioning the jaw joint in front of the cheek horn tip in lateral view, a feature not reported in other ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: Akainacephalus johnsoni is known for being the most complete ankylosaur specimen found in southern Laramidia, including a complete skull, tail, osteoderms, limb elements, and part of the pelvis.

facts.statement: The area covering the frontal and nasal bones is covered by symmetrical, pyramid-shaped caputegulae, indicating a specific armor pattern.

facts.statement: Fossils of Akainacephalus are known from the middle unit of the Kaiparowits Formation, dated to the upper Campanian at 76.26 ± 0.10 million years ago.
